llm.summary: This is a disclosed ScraperSocial/Naver API wrapper that sends user-supplied searches to ScraperSocial and does not show hidden persistence, local data access, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The scripts require SCRAPERSOCIAL_KEY and outbound requests to api.scrapersocial.com, which fits the API-wrapper purpose; users should understand their queries and parameters leave the local environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package install, dependency download, remote code execution, or installer behavior was present; the artifact contains only Node scripts and documentation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The generic call_endpoint.js is broader than the four named search scripts, but it is disclosed in SKILL.md and constrained in code to paths beginning with /v1/naver/.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, scheduled jobs, shell spawning, credential-store scraping, file mutation, or privilege escalation behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is public Naver search via ScraperSocial, and the scripts implement blog, cafe article, local, shopping, plus a documented generic /v1/naver/ endpoint caller.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable sending Naver search terms and parameters to ScraperSocial using your SCRAPERSOCIAL_KEY. Avoid submitting secrets, personal data, or confidential research terms unless ScraperSocial's privacy and retention practices meet your needs.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The generic endpoint caller is real, but it is documented in the scripts table and restricted by code to /v1/naver/ paths, so it is a disclosed API escape hatch rather than hidden tool poisoning.
[LP3] expected: The skill does not include a separate allowed-tools section, but its environment variable and API use are disclosed in frontmatter and setup; no broad local authority was found.
[SQP-2] expected: Queries are sent to ScraperSocial as part of the stated API-wrapper function. A clearer privacy notice would be helpful, but the third-party API relationship is disclosed.
